title: Products of Hermite polynomials of two unit Gaussian projections
status: Authored natural statement and topology for reuse/admission review; not an independent source verdict
scope: One existing generic Hermite product theorem. No new proof search or model-specific assumptions.

assumptions.text: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space. Its measurable structure is the Borel structure. Completeness is derivable from finite dimension.
u,v are vectors in E with ||u||=||v||=1. The two directions need not be independent, distinct, orthogonal, or non-collinear.
m,n are arbitrary natural numbers, including zero.

definitions.text: gamma=stdGaussian(E), the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance on the actual ambient space E.

H_k is the probabilists Hermite polynomial over the integers, evaluated in reals by the canonical coefficient map. Its defining recursion is H_0=1 and H_(k+1)(t)=t H_k(t)-H_k′(t). This is the unnormalized convention, with leading coefficient one.
rho=<u,v> is the actual inner product, not an independent parameter. G(x)=H_m(<u,x>) H_n(<v,x>) is a literal real-valued function.

conclusion.text: G is absolutely Bochner integrable under gamma and integral_E G(x)d gamma(x) equals n! rho^n when m=n, and zero when m!=n.
conclusion.formula: integral H_m(<u,x>) H_n(<v,x>) d gamma(x) = indicator(m=n) n! <u,v>^n.
conclusion.quantifier_order: E and its structures; u,v and both unit hypotheses; m,n; product integrability and the exact integral identity. There are no integrability, covariance, differentiation or orthogonality assumptions beyond A1-A3.
conclusion.encoding_note: The existing exact Lean signature uses indices i,j and returns i!<u,v>^i in the i=j branch. This is the same formula as n!rho^n in the equal-degree case; no theorem statement change is proposed.

edge_cases.text: m=n=0 gives one, including rho=0, because the exponent is a natural zeroth power.
All rho in [-1,1] induced by unit vectors are included. At u=v the equal-degree value is n!; at u=-v it is n!(-1)^n. No division by 1-rho² is used.

Dimension one and coincident/antipodal directions are allowed. In dimension zero there are no unit vectors, so the theorem has vacuous hypotheses; it does not assert a nonexistent unit Gaussian projection.
The identity is an exact scalar integral, not a pointwise identity, independence assertion, or almost-everywhere equality of the two factors.

proof_topology.text: Existing Gaussian polynomial L2 membership makes every polynomial ridge square-integrable. Cauchy–Schwarz supplies integrability of products of two ridges, including a linear factor absorbed into one polynomial.

Reuse the existing staged Gaussian Stein theorem for f(x)=H_i(<u,x>)q(<v,x>) in direction u. The theorem requires differentiability and integrability of f, <x,u>f, and its directional derivative; all are derived for these polynomials using T1 and the polynomial chain/product rules.

The directional derivative is H_i′(<u,x>)q(<v,x>)+rho H_i(<u,x>)q′(<v,x>). The first term cancels the negative derivative in the Hermite recursion. Hence integral H_(i+1)(<u,x>)q(<v,x>) = rho integral H_i(<u,x>)q′(<v,x>).
Iterate to obtain integral H_i(<u,x>)q(<v,x>) = rho^i integral q^(i)(<v,x>). This uses polynomial derivatives and no conditional Gaussian or nondegeneracy hypothesis.
For i=j, monicity and degree imply H_i^(i)=i!, so the Gaussian probability integral is i!. For i>j, H_j^(i)=0. These calculations include degree zero.

If i<j, exchange the two factors and directions, apply T5 using the second unit hypothesis, and commute the inner product in the equal-degree case. Together with T1 this gives both claimed conclusions.

source_boundary: This generic supplement states only the Hermite covariance identity. Finite feature sums, feature derivative bounds, series limits, tangent gradients and force estimates are downstream consumers and receive no admission credit here.
authorship_note: This topology is an authored reconstruction from the exact mathematical proposition and existing staged proof. Independent source review remains separate.
